external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: Colleagues sign in from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state where franchise colleagues are located.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider used by franchise colleagues to vouch for their identities.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, maintains directory membership, signs tokens, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in. Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires. The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log. Whether colleagues are asked for a second factor is not documented.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that lets holders of a store-manager token change prices and void transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

processes.name: HR system
processes.description: The system from which group membership changes are pulled overnight.
processes.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.
processes.notes: The source does not state where the HR system runs.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Whether the directory is encrypted where it sits has not been written down.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. Whether the log is encrypted where it sits has not been written down.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague initiates sign-in with the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: vouch
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to the store admin console for authorization decisions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in. The same key signs tokens for every application.
data_flows.data_description: token containing the colleague's staff id and groups

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: public half of the token signing key

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls HR group membership changes overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The same overnight pull is how leavers stop being colleagues.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker updates its directory with colleague and group membership information.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key it uses to sign tokens from the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: write sign-in
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: It is not documented what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The store admin console is also stated to run on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's colleague and group membership records are confidential because they contain staff identity and membership information.
assumptions.basis: The directory keeps colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's signing key is confidential because it is a signing secret.
assumptions.basis: The key store holds the signing key used by the broker to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's sign-in records are confidential because they record colleague sign-ins.
assumptions.basis: The broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console presents a web interface because it is described as a console application used by colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source names the process 'store admin console'; console is treated as a web application interface under the extraction convention.
